title: urnetwork / signals
description: The SIGNALS.md signal catalog plus the operator network measurements, charted. Panel titles carry the section numbers where applicable; panel descriptions carry the measurement semantics and playbook pointers. Loaded by `bringyourctl grafana load-defaults`.

panels.title: 2.7 new connections / min
panels.description: The new-connection rate (SIGNALS.md 2.7). Two failure directions: sustained < 50% of the trailing baseline = new connects failing (auth/lb/announce); sustained > 2.5x = a RECONNECT STORM — mass simultaneous eviction (ansible unit-restart wave 8.5, simultaneous multi-block deploy). During a storm expect a plateau, a final eviction burst spike, then decay to baseline ~10 min after.

panels.title: 1.1 transfer throughput (contract-path proxy)
panels.description: Bytes acked through closed/checkpointed transfer contracts — the mimir-side proxy for the 1.1 contract-creation rate (the exact per-minute pg rate lives in the monitor). A cliff = systemic; a sag = partial failure; a ramp = recovery.

panels.title: population: client transport connections
panels.description: Open client transports. One distinct resident device may have multiple transports, so this is intentionally not labeled as a device count; the operator-measurements row below charts resident devices.

panels.title: §4 contract failures / min by cause + companion (lossless)
panels.description: urnetwork_connect_contract_failures_total — the lossless counter behind the sampled contract-error log exemplars. missing_companion_origin climbing while everything else is healthy = stale provider selection serving zombies (playbook 5.9; post-churn variant 5.9.7). insufficient_balance step-change = netEscrow drift re-emerging (§4). Empty until the instrumented api build deploys.

panels.title: 2.8-adjacent: findproviders2 sample drops / s
panels.description: Selection-path pressure signal. Selection FRESHNESS (2.8, the UpdateClientScores completion gap and cs_ ttls) is pg/redis-side and lives in the monitor.

panels.title: service readiness (processes reporting ready)
panels.description: A step DOWN that does not recover within a deploy window = processes dying (crash-loop playbook 5.10: confirm with docker ps Exited churn on one build tag).

panels.title: 1.4-adjacent: redis pool timeouts / s by service
panels.description: App-side redis backpressure (3.5): pool timeouts mean something is slow consuming the pool — find the slow node/command (per-node view: urnetwork / redis cluster; §5.2/5.3 batteries live in the monitor).

panels.title: log signal taxonomy (SIGNALS.md §4) — all services, lines/min
§4 page-tier classes / min
panels.description: First-match taxonomy from the monitor tailers. dial-io-timeout = accept-path starvation (5.2); connection-refused = process dead / wrong interface (5.2); clusterdown = slot coverage lost (5.3); oom-writes = node at maxmemory, writes fail while reads work (5.4); panic = read the innermost app frame.

panels.title: §4 warn-tier classes / min

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({env="$env"} |~ `channel is full for .* \(message is dropped\)` [1m]))
sum(count_over_time({env="$env"} |~ `asset amount owned by the wallet is insufficient|insufficient token balance .* in wallet` [1m]))

panels.description: port-exhaustion self-drains ~60s after its target is fixed; redis-loading only matters sustained > 2 min; payout-wallet = fund the wallet (finance, not a bug); drain-gave-up = check stranded task leases (12.1).

panels.title: §4 contract-error exemplars / min (sampled logs)
panels.description: SAMPLED log exemplars (the api rate-limits these lines) — judge rates from the lossless contract-failures counter above once the instrumented build is live.

panels.title: novel error-shaped volume / min by service
panels.description: Cheap approximation of the monitor's `novel` classifier (the full word-boundary regex times out in loki at fleet volume). A NEW sustained band that no §4 class explains is the novel signal — drill in with urnetwork / service logs; the monitor normalizes and samples the exact shapes.

panels.title: connect drain: residents remaining
panels.description: Nonzero = a connect block is draining (deploy/rebalance walking residents off, 8.2). MANY blocks nonzero at once = a simultaneous restart wave (8.5), not a rolling deploy.

panels.title: drain excuses written / consumed / s
panels.description: CONNECTDRAIN2 track A: drain-caused disruption marked at the source and excused at reliability ingest. written without consumed = the excusal is not reaching ingest.

panels.title: service drain state
panels.description: Live drain progress. HTTP draining counts instances in their drain sequence; the remaining series show work that still has to leave each service. Completed-drain outcomes are charted below because final gauges are brief before their process series goes stale.

panels.title: 8.1 running versions (build_info)
panels.description: The publish-side deploy clock. The authoritative deploy state is the containers on the edges (docker ps, 8.1) — a fix is live only once the OLD build tag is gone (8.2/8.3).

panels.title: 9 dispatched key events / s
panels.description: Should track registry churn (connects/disconnects/provide changes; hop opens/closes). Flat DURING churn = events not arriving (notify-keyspace-events off on a node — 9.1 class-set check — or the subscriber is down).

panels.title: 9 subscription health / s
panels.description: Resubscribes: one per process start; sustained = conn deaths or topology flapping. Listener resets should be ≈ registrations + resyncs; sustained excess = the corrective poll is repairing dropped events — find the drop first.

panels.title: 9 key-event merge drops / s
panels.description: In-process consumer stall on the key-event channel (pairs with the §4 pubsub-drops log class, playbook 5.5).

panels.title: total networks
panels.description: Total networks registered with this operator. The collector runs on every taskworker, so max — not sum or avg — selects the replicated measurement without replica-count or unset-gauge skew.

panels.title: countries with a connected provider
panels.description: Countries with at least one connected, valid public provider. This measures provider reach, not consuming-device locations.

panels.title: connected devices (residents)
panels.description: Distinct resident client devices across connect processes. This differs from connected_clients, which counts transport connections and can count one device more than once.

panels.title: weekly users: current vs last finished block
panels.description: Unique top-level identities with contract usage. The current accumulator resets at 00:00 UTC Sunday; the previous series is the final value of the last finished block and is absent until one has been observed.

panels.title: weekly demand deposits: current vs last finished block
panels.description: Alpha demand deposits measured from the mirrored contract events for the current weekly block and the last finished block.

panels.title: weekly miner emissions: current vs last finished block
panels.description: Alpha miner emission captured from the mirrored contract events for the current weekly block and the last finished block.

panels.title: cumulative alpha staked
panels.description: Cumulative alpha staked in the subnet contract (buybackTotal). No data means the chain measurement is not currently being published; it is not converted to zero.

panels.title: alpha price (USD)
panels.description: Alpha price in US dollars from the operator's server-side market observation. The collector retains the last good value across a transient price-source error.

panels.title: online public providers
panels.description: Connected valid providers holding a public provide key — the population behind the public providers map and the public dashboard's country map. Every taskworker publishes the same measurement, so max selects it without replica skew.

panels.title: provider reach: regions + cities
panels.description: Distinct regions and cities with a connected valid public provider, from the same scan as the country count.

panels.title: users last 24h
panels.description: Unique top-level identities with contract usage in the trailing 24 hours (the block users predicate over a rolling window).

panels.title: providers by country (top 10)
panels.description: The per-country provider gauge behind the public dashboard's map, top 10 by count. Series for a country that lost its last provider are deleted by the collector on the next refresh, so they go stale rather than pushing a stale count forever.

panels.title: weekly miner claims: current vs last finished block
panels.description: Alpha claimed by miners (MinerClaimed events in the st_event mirror) inside the weekly block window.

panels.title: miners claiming: current vs last finished block
panels.description: Distinct miner coldkeys with a MinerClaimed event inside the weekly block window.

panels.title: subnet block clock
panels.description: The block clock the collector publishes for the public dashboard's progress gauge: the 1-based block number and the current block's open and close unix times (as seconds relative to now here). A flat block number with a sawtooth remaining time is healthy; a jump at any time other than Sunday 00:00 UTC is a clock or collector fault.

panels.title: connect control failures / s
panels.description: Lossless bounded-label counters for rejected control frames and resident nominations. Split control-frame failures by message and cause; split nomination refusals by cause.

panels.title: authentication decisions / s
panels.description: JWTs rejected by bounded cause, and JWTs accepted only because a migration gate still permits a legacy condition. Legacy accepts should reach zero before the corresponding gate is removed.

panels.title: contract + task terminal outcomes / s
panels.description: Expired contracts force-closed by resolution, plus RunPost tasks whose finished-task row had already been reaped. The orphaned task outcome is a safe no-op, but any sustained rate merits retention/scheduling investigation.

panels.title: FindProviders2 score-load latency
panels.description: Distribution of the client-score load performed by every provider search. Quantiles are computed from the merged fleet histogram, not averaged from per-process quantiles.

panels.title: message pool lifecycle / s
panels.description: Pooled buffers taken, returned, and newly allocated. Taken and returned should track; created tracking taken means the pool is not reusing buffers effectively.

panels.title: unpooled message allocations
panels.description: Oversize messages served outside the fixed-size pools, shown as messages/s and bytes/s on separate axes.

panels.title: completed drain duration
panels.description: Duration reported at the end of each HTTP or taskworker drain. The five-minute lookback keeps the final flush visible briefly after its process series goes stale.

panels.title: work interrupted at drain completion
panels.description: HTTP connections still open at the hard shutdown deadline and task executions canceled then rescheduled by taskworker drain. Both should normally be zero; canceled tasks are recoverable, hard-cut connections are not graceful.

panels.title: proxy device resources and return-path pressure
proxy DeviceLocal memory and carrier bytes
panels.description: Fleet totals for the per-device steady-state memory target, tracked live use, private platform-carrier budget and use, and H1 bytes waiting for carrier admission. Tracked use excludes allocator/runtime and bounded NAT endpoint memory. Sustained pending H1 bytes with used carrier bytes at budget indicates carrier starvation rather than provider reachability.

panels.title: proxy platform-carrier admission
panels.description: Fleet carrier slots: private per-device limits, acquired carriers, and H1 reservations waiting for admission. The limit should scale with live hosted devices; a flat limit while device count grows indicates a stale shared-budget build. Sustained pending H1 at the limit is the direct carrier-starvation signature.

panels.title: proxy WireGuard return backpressure / s
panels.description: Returned WireGuard packets that had to wait for the fixed receive queue. A rising count means bounded flow control was applied rather than dropping the packet; correlate sustained events with wait duration and process lifecycle.

panels.title: proxy WireGuard return backpressure duration
panels.description: Fleet histogram of time spent waiting for bounded WireGuard receive-queue capacity. Quantiles are computed after merging histogram buckets across instances; the mean uses the merged sum and count.

panels.title: signals not on this board (and where they live)

options.content:
Grafana sees only **warp-mimir** and **warp-loki**, so pg-backed and ssh-backed signals cannot be charted here — they run in the monitor (`server/monitor`, SIGNALS.md is the catalog):

- **1.1 pg contract rate / 1.2 canary + task health (§7, §12) / 1.3 active vs idle-in-tx state split / 2.x tier-1 pg (open-set, vacuum, stats landmine, task durations) / 2.8 selection freshness** — pg via ssh; no pg datasource is provisioned.
- **§3 per-node redis internals** — `urnetwork / redis cluster` charts the redis_* exporter series; the slowlog/latency/keyspace batteries (5.2–5.4, 3.3 family histogram, 9.1 config checks) are monitor-side redis-cli.
- **§5 escalation batteries, §8 container-level deploy state** — ssh/docker on the edges.

Related boards: `urnetwork / redis cluster` (§3), `urnetwork / host metrics`, `urnetwork / services overview` (process vitals + versions), `urnetwork / service logs` (drill-in).
